source.method: yt-dlp flat channel enumeration + oEmbed identity sweep + LLM title-to-spec adjudication; evidence is TITLE-ONLY (no high rows); tightened binding rule (title must name the spec's distinctive content); sewage filter applied (promo/announcement/non-teaching uploads excluded)

review.task: T-VIDEOMAP-P4 (shelf-direct lane, Cognito maths shelf: cie-igcse-maths-25-extended)
review.ruling: delegated self-review — owner chat 2026-11-09: 'For now, approve and review yourself'
review.reviewer: delegated self-review (agent, per owner chat 2026-11-09: 'approve and review yourself')
review.evidenceBasis: Checked every mapping row of the 118-row draft against the cie-igcse-maths-25-extended spine (title-only evidence; per-(video,spec) judging; physics-branded rows judged on whether the title names the spec's own clause). Rejected 4 spec-level bindings: two factorising-quadratics videos riding along on E2.5.6 (titles name factorising, not solving quadratics), a plotting-inequalities video riding on E2.6.4 (title names plotting, not listing inequalities that define a region), and 'Similar Shapes' on E4.4.2 (title names the similarity domain, not the lengths/areas/volumes scale-factor frame the evidence itself marks 'only supporting'). All other low rows were kept only where the partial support names a clause genuinely in the spec (e.g. travel graphs, best value, fractional indices).

rejects.reason: 'Factorising Quadratics - Part 1 - (When the x² Coefficient is 1)' names the factorisation technique that is E2.2.4's own spec; E2.5.6's distinctive frame is 'Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, completing the square and by use of the quadratic formula' — no solving, completing the square or formula is title-evidenced. Ride-along on the E2.2.4 binding; rejected at medium.

'Factorising Quadratics - Part 2 - (When the x² Coefficient is More Than 1)' same pattern: title names factorising expressions (E2.2.4), not the solve-quadratic-equations frame of E2.5.6. Ride-along; rejected at medium.

'Solving Inequalities by Plotting them on a Graph' names plotting inequalities on a graph, which is E2.6.3's exact topic; E2.6.4's distinctive task is the reverse direction — 'List inequalities that define a given region' (linear programming) — not title-evidenced. Ride-along on the E2.6.3 binding; rejected at medium.

'Similar Shapes' names the similarity domain (E4.4.1's lengths frame and E4.4.3's problem-solving survive), but E4.4.2's distinctive frame is 'relationships between lengths and areas ... surface areas and volumes of similar solids' (k/k²/k³ scale factors) — the evidence itself marks the area/volume relationships 'only supporting', i.e. not title-evidenced. Same pattern as the owner's 4.16-style identity rejects.
